scenes.headline: How a dense 65B model fits on a desk
scenes.sub: Ripple-65B Preview, read from its file headers.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Tidepool! Ripple is a new open model where every weight runs for every token. Here is how it is built, and how it fits on a desk.

scenes.text: A dense model built thin and deep: 80 narrow layers, mostly short local attention, and values that reach back to the token itself.
scenes.mark: values that reach back to the token itself
scenes.say: The idea: eighty narrow layers, mostly short local attention, and values that reach back to the token itself.

steps.say: A token enters a layer. Its queries and keys come from the layer's input, with twice the heads the width needs.
The values are different. Each layer blends its input with the original token embedding, using one learned number.
Early and late layers take most of their values from the embedding. The middle layers ignore it.
A sigmoid gates the attention output. Then a very wide MLP, which holds most of the weights, does the rest.

steps.label: sliding layer, 1,024 tokens
steps.say: Four of every five layers look back only a short window. Their cache stops growing.

steps.label: global layer, no positions
steps.say: Every fifth layer sees the whole context, with no position encoding. Only these sixteen keep every token.

scenes.title: Weight files against a DGX Spark
scenes.say: Now the bytes. Full precision is bigger than the box. The official Spark build makes only the MLPs four bit.

left.title: Plain decoding
left.say: A dense model reads every weight for every token. That caps plain decoding near five tokens a second.

right.title: With the DFlash2 drafter
items: Drafts a block, verifies in one pass
right.say: A small drafter guesses a block and the big model checks it in one pass. On code, that runs five times faster.

scenes.text: A dense model on a desk is a memory-bandwidth problem, and the drafter is what buys the speed.
scenes.mark: the drafter is what buys the speed
scenes.say: On a desk, a dense model is a bandwidth problem, and the drafter is what buys the speed.

recap: Values blend back to the token embedding
Four sliding layers, then one global
scenes.say: Values that reach back to the token. Short memory in most layers. Four-bit MLPs on one Spark.
